transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-09-02
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Olivia Hart (Head of ML, Spectra), Marcus Lee (CTO, Spectra), Anita Rao (FinOps Manager, Spectra)

Auto-generated Summary: medium quality transcription; some words may be slightly off.

00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, really appreciate the time. quick round-robin - Maya from Redwood, Liam my solutions engineer.
00:06 Olivia: Hi, Olivia here - Head of ML at Spectra Finance. Marcus and Anita also with me.
00:10 Marcus: yep hey all.
00:12 Liam: great, we're primarily here to understand your workloads and cost constraints so we can recommend hosted vs dedicated vs private.
00:22 Anita: yes, top line - we run user-facing summarization and a few rerank tasks, roughly 1M tokens/day today, expected to grow 3x in six months. budget is tight, FinOps wants unit economics visibility.
00:35 Maya: ok good, that's perfect context. Quick question on latency SLOs — what are you targeting for summaries?
00:40 Olivia: sub-800ms p50 ideally, p95 <2s for end-user flows. rerank can be higher latency, up to 5s is ok for batch jobs.
00:48 Liam: good. Some quick product framing - Redwood Hosted is our fastest route and simple per-token billing; Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput and lower unit costs when you commit; Private is mostly for data residency/regulatory constraints and has different pricing.
01:05 Marcus: can you give ballpark per-token numbers? our finance team wants concrete figures to compare with current OpenAI spend.
01:12 Maya: absolutely - I'll caveat these as starting points. Hosted vanilla GPT-ish model variants — our list price is around $0.004 to $0.02 per 1k tokens depending on the model family and context length. For embeddings it's separate. With batching and KV cache we typically reduce effective cost per token by 20-40% depending on hit rates.
01:35 Anita: sorry can you repeat the hosted range, I missed the lower end?
01:38 Maya: sure — roughly $0.004 to $0.02 per 1k tokens on hosted for the common open-ish models we serve. If you do a Dedicated reserved commit, unit price can drop, roughly another 30-50% off that hosted list price depending on commitment level and utilization.
01:55 Olivia: 30-50% is significant. how do you get that reduction — is it pure compute amortization or architecture differences?
02:02 Liam: mix of both. Dedicated amortizes GPU cost with reserved capacity and we also tune batching aggressively: continuous batching across requests, longer batch windows for non-latency-sensitive flows, and model quantization options. The runtime also uses prefix/KV caching for repeated context which lowers repeated compute. In practice, if you have a high prefix reuse rate, effective tokens billed for compute drop.
02:25 Marcus: can you quantify caching impact? we have many similar prompts — paraphrases mostly.
02:29 Liam: if your prefix reuse is high, say 40-60% cache hit on the KV, you can see 25-40% effective compute reduction. But it depends on sequence length distribution and how much of the token stream is cacheable.
02:42 Anita: how about batching tradeoffs — won't batching increase p95? we care about tail latency for user flows.
02:48 Liam: yes there's a tradeoff. For low-latency routes we use small max batch sizes and aggressive timeouts to keep p95 down; for background reranking we batch bigger and accept higher latency to get much lower per-token compute. You can also route by policy — split user flows to a low-latency pool and batchable jobs to dedicated queues.
03:07 Olivia: ok, that routing sounds useful. For numbers — say our 1M tokens/day, what's the rough monthly cost hosted vs dedicated?
03:16 Maya: quick rough math here — at $0.01 per 1k tokens baseline hosted -> 1M tokens/day is about 30M tokens/month -> 30k units of 1k tokens -> $300 monthly at $0.01? wait, math check — actually 30M tokens = 30,000 * 1k tokens -> yes $300. But that seems low so I might've mis-communicated; depends on model choice and whether prompts+responses counted etc. If you use a larger model at $0.02 per 1k tokens that's $600. With Dedicated, say 40% reduction, that could be $180-360. BUT note that dedicated pricing often has a base reserved capacity monthly fee and minimum commits, so small teams might not see immediate savings until utilization is high.
03:56 Marcus: that makes sense. we need a precise worksheet we can plug our prompt lengths and tokenization metrics into.
04:03 Maya: we'll produce a benchmark sheet. Liam: can you outline what you'll need from them?
04:08 Liam: sure — ideally: sample prompt mix, average input and output tokens per API call, concurrency profile, acceptable latency targets per route, and expected growth curve. With that we can model costs for Hosted, Dedicated with different commit levels, and a Private deployment TCO.
04:24 Anita: about Private — we have some compliance work coming up for certain clients; private deployment might be required. What's the TCO delta?
04:30 Liam: Private has higher up-front setup and licensing; you pay for the control plane on-prem or VPC plus support. Unit costs can be lower if you manage high utilization on your infra, but there's ops overhead. For banking/regulatory use-cases we often see customers go Private when they need full control over network egress or air-gapped setups.
04:47 Olivia: and encryption/KMS - is data encrypted at rest and do you support customer-managed keys?
04:51 Maya: yes, Hosted supports encryption at rest and in-transit; we integrate with customer KMS for Dedicated and Private, and Private gives you full control with HSM/KMS options. We'll share the SOC2 and KMS docs in the follow-up.
05:02 Marcus: do you do per-route RBAC? our product has strict access controls for model rollout.
05:06 Liam: yes, RBAC, SSO/SAML integrations, audit logs — those are standard enterprise features on Dedicated and Private; hosted also supports SSO and audit events but with different retention tiers.
05:17 Olivia: back on cost — can you run sensitivity for batching windows? if we increase batching window from 20ms to 100ms what is trade-off?
05:24 Liam: sure, roughly speaking longer batching windows increase per-request latency but improve throughput and lower cost per token. For a traffic profile with 200 requests/sec, moving to 100ms windows may get you 15-25% better batching efficiency depending on burstiness. We'll simulate in the spreadsheet.
05:40 Anita: what about quantization — can you run smaller models but quantized to reduce cost and keep quality?
05:45 Liam: yes, we recommend quantized variants for Dedicated; 4-bit/8-bit quantization reduces memory and throughput cost. There's sometimes a small accuracy hit; we can run evals on your prompt sets to validate.
05:58 Olivia: what's the POC scope you're proposing?
06:01 Maya: typical POC — 2 weeks, we run a benchmark with your sample prompts, measure latency, throughput, and cost across Hosted and a Dedicated-like config. We'll provide a notebook/spreadsheet and a short runbook to replicate.
06:14 Marcus: are there any hidden costs — egress, storage, extra infra for caching?
06:19 Liam: egress is standard cloud egress; for Dedicated we include model cache and KV cache as part of the runtime. If you want longer-term prefix stores or extra observability retention that's an add-on. We'll call those out explicitly in the quote.
06:34 Anita: ok, FinOps wants a monthly forecast for budgets — best and worst case.
06:39 Maya: we'll produce a baseline, optimistic (with caching/batching savings), and pessimistic (no caching, peak model choice) scenarios.
06:48 Olivia: any concerns around multi-tenant hosted versus dedicated isolation? some clients ask about data separation.
06:54 Liam: Hosted is logically multi-tenant with strong isolation, but Dedicated gives you isolated GPU pools and data separation guarantees. Private is the only fully self-managed option.
07:05 Marcus: competitor question — we've been comparing to OpenAI and Vertex. how do you typically position Redwood on price and performance?
07:11 Maya: we position on predictable unit economics and production controls — with similar or better per-token costs after optimization, plus better observability and rollout controls. For some noisy workloads OpenAI can be simpler but lacks the same dedicated capacity options. Vertex can be competitive at scale — we'll show comparative benchmarks in the pricing sheet but caution it's workload dependent.
07:28 Olivia: great. Anything else we should prepare?
07:31 Liam: send the 3 sample workloads, concurrency, and any special compliance checklist. We'll queue the benchmark and cost modeling once we have that.
07:38 Maya: recap: we'll send pricing sheet, SOC2/KMS docs, benchmark template and proposed POC plan. Action items as noted.
07:46 Anita: sounds good, thanks.
07:48 Marcus: thanks all.
07:50 Olivia: thanks, bye.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings corrected inline; speaker labels are best-effort. The transcript includes negotiation details: hosted per-1k-token ranges, estimated Dedicated discounts, batching/cache quantification ranges and POC commitments.
